Numbered equations (1.1)-(1.3) are named formulas (Weber's, Hardy's, and their complex analogue proved in Qi's papers), so retyped as external theorems.

The inline 'We claim' in the proof of Lemma 6.1 is followed first by the use of the claim and only later by its proof ('We now show the absolute convergence'); the claim step was not nested over the following sentences, and the proof of the claim is a separate parent step with three children.
Lemma 2.1 is justified by a prose paragraph that restates the Jacquet-Shalika expansion; the paragraph is the proof node and the restated result is a nested external theorem.

Historical and expository prose in Sections 1 and 4, the informal introduction of i_{pi,psi1} and j_{sigma,psi1} before Theorem 1.1, the intro copy of the definition of boldface J, and the intro preview of the theta-correspondence remark (kept as RP4) are not separate nodes.

The phrase 'the deduction from (1.3) to (6.1)' was read by the finishing step as a reference range and produced uses edges from every equation labelled in between; these 23 spurious edges were removed after finalize, keeping only the three real references (as mentions).

Lemma 6.1 says 'where hat f_2 is the psi-Fourier transform of f_2' but the formula uses hat f_3 (typo kept verbatim). The appendix propositions have proofs omitted, deferred to Baruch-Mao's real case, hence semi_formal.

nodes.name: Local integrability of the Bessel function j
nodes.statement:
Assume that $\pi $ is unitary. Then $j $ is locally integrable over $G$. Namely, for any $f\in C_c^\infty(G)$, we have
\[
\int_G \left|f(g)j (g) \right| dg<\infty.
\]
conclusions: $j $ is locally integrable over $G$.

nodes.name: Proof of local integrability of j
nodes.statement:
Recall that the measure on $X = NA \varw_0 N$ is given by $ d g = |a|^{-2} d x \hskip 1 pt d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  a   \hskip 1 pt d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt c \hskip 1 pt d y$ if $g = n(x)z(c)t(a)\varw_0n(y)$. We have
\begin{align*}
 \int_G |f(g)j (g)| dg
= \ & \int_{X}|f(g)j (g)|dg \\
= \ &\int |j (t(a)\varw_0)|\left(\iiint |f(n(x)z(c)t(a)\varw_0n(y))|dxdyd^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  c \right) |a|^{-2}d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  a \\
= \ & \int |j (t(a)\varw_0)| \left (  \int  J \big( \sqrt a,   c, |f| \big)    d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  c  \right ) |a|^{-2} d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  a,
\end{align*}
where $ J \big( \sqrt a,   c, |f| \big) $ is the orbital integral defined as in \eqref{def: J (a,c,f)}.  In view of Proposition \ref{prop:A1},  the inner integral over $c$ is zero for small $|a|$    and of the order $|a|^{1+\varepsilon}$ for large  $|a|$. In view of  Lemma \ref{4lem: bounds for J} and the expression of $j = j_{\pi, \hskip 0.5 pt \psi}$ as in \eqref{4eq : j = J}, $j   (t(a) \varw_0)$ is bounded by $ {|a|}^{\frac 1 2}$ when $|a|$ is large. It is now clear that the integral above is convergent.
nodes.statement_short: Integrate over Bruhat coordinates; the $(N,N)$ orbital integral vanishes for small $|a|$ and is $O(|a|^{1+\varepsilon})$, while $j$ grows at most like $|a|^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement:
The proof is similar to that of   \cite[Lemma 7.1]{BaruchMao-Real}.
   For any $\varv\in H_\infty$, we have
   \begin{align*}
    \pi(\rho_r(t(a))f) \varv 
    & =    \int_G f(gt(a))\pi(g) \varv \hskip 0.5 pt dg \\
    & =\int_G f(g)\pi(g)\pi(t(a^{-1})) \varv\hskip 0.5 pt dg = \pi (f) \pi(t(a^{-1})) \varv.
   \end{align*}
   Thus it follow from  \eqref{def: vector v l f}, \eqref{def: J (f)} and \eqref{def: Wv(g)} that $\varv_{L,\hskip 1 pt \rho_r(t(a))f}=\pi(t(a))\varv_{L, \hskip 0.5 pt f}$ and $J (\rho_r(t(a))f)=\overline {W_{\varv_{L, \hskip 0.5 pt f}}(t(a))}$. Hence, in view of \eqref{eq: inner product}, we have
   \[
   \int_{{\mathbb {C}}^{\times}} J (\rho_r(t(a))f)W_\varv(t(a))d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  a=\langle \varv,\varv_{L, \hskip 0.5 pt f} \rangle.
   \]
   On the other hand, by \eqref{def: vector v l f} and \eqref{def: Wv(g)},
   \[
   \langle \varv,\varv_{L, \hskip 0.5 pt f} \rangle =L(\pi(f)\varv)=\int_G f(g)W_\varv(g)dg,
   \]
   which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Translate the test function to get $J(\rho_r(t(a))f)=\overline{W_{v_{L,f}}(t(a))}$, then use the inner product formula (3.1).

&= \int_{X} f(g) \left( \int  j (gt(a^{-1}))W_\varv(t(a))d^{\times} \hskip -1 pt  a \right)dg  \\
&= \int_{X} f(g)W_\varv(g)dg.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5.3

nodes.name: Proof of full regularity of I
nodes.statement:
Let $T$ be the distribution on $G$ defined by the difference $T=I-\widetilde I$. First, in view of \eqref{6eq: I = int of i},  $I$ and $\widetilde I$ coincide on $X$, so $T$ is supported on the Borel $B = G\smallsetminus X$. Second, it is clear that $T$ satisfies  $\rho_r(n(y))I=\psi(y)I$. Third, we claim that $T$ is an eigen-distribution of  the Casimir element $\varDelta$ in the universal enveloping algebra of the Lie algebra of $G$. To see this, we first note that  $I$ is an eigen-distribution of $\varDelta$ according to \cite[\S 3]{Shalika-MO}, that is,  $\varDelta I= \kappa I$ ($\kappa \in {\mathbb {C}}$). As aforementioned, $I$ is represented by the (real analytic) function $i$ when restricted on $ U $, so $i$ is an eigen-function of $\varDelta$  on $U$.

nodes.name: Proof of the main theorem
nodes.statement: The proof is a simple comparison between the formulae \eqref{4eq: j = J, SL} and \eqref{6eq: defn of i}. To verify the equality,  it should be noted that by \cite[(4.7)]{Knapp} and \cite[\S 3]{Tate} we have $\epsilon (\pi, s, \psi_{\lambdaup}) = i^{|m|} \omega_{\pi} (\lambdaup) \|\lambdaup\|^{2s -1}$ if $\pi = \pi_{\mu, \hskip 0.5 pt  m}$, and hence $\epsilon (\pi, 1/2, \psi_{\lambdaup}) = i^{|m|} = (-1)^{\frac 1 2 m}$ when $m$ is even so that $\omega_{\pi} (\lambdaup) = 1$. Note that $\epsilon (\pi, 1/2, \psi)$ is actually independent on $\psi$.

nodes.name: The correspondence is Waldspurger's theta correspondence
nodes.statement: We remark that $ \sigma = \Theta (\pi) = \Theta (\pi , \psi^D)$ according to the notation of the theta correspondence of Waldspurger \cite{Waldspurger-Shimura}. Unlike the real case (see \cite[Theorem 19.2]{BaruchMao-Real}),  here $\sigma$    is independent on the additive character $\psi^D$.
nodes.statement_short: $\sigma=\Theta(\pi,\psi^D)$ is Waldspurger's theta lift and, unlike the real case, independent of $\psi^D$.

nodes.name: Jacquet's matching of orbital integrals
nodes.statement:
It is proven in \cite{Jacquet-RTF} that for each $f \in C_c^\infty (G)$ there exists $f' \in C_c^\infty (S)$ such that
\begin{equation} O^{A, \hskip 0.5 pt N}_{f, \hskip 0.5 pt \psi} (n(z/4D) \varw_0) = O^{N, \hskip 0.5 pt N}_{f', \hskip 0.5 pt \psi^D} (\varw s(z)) \psi (-2D/z) {\textstyle \sqrt {\|z\|}}/ \gamma (z, \psi^D),

for all $z \in {\mathbb {C}}^{\times}$.

nodes.name: Distributional Bessel identity
nodes.statement_short: For matching $f,f'$ and corresponding $\pi,\sigma$, $I_{\pi,\psi}(f)$ equals $J_{\sigma,\psi^D}(f')$ times $\epsilon/\|2D\|L$.

nodes.name: (N,N) orbital integral J(a,c,f)
J(a,c,f)
nodes.statement: J(a,c,f)=\iint f(n(x)z(c)s(a)\varw_0n(y))dxdy.
nodes.label: def: J (a,c,f)

nodes.name: Properties of (N,N) orbital integrals
nodes.statement:
Let $f\in C_c (G)$. Then

{\rm(1).} $J(a,c,f)$ converges absolutely for all $a,c\in {\mathbb {C}}^{\times}$.

{\rm(2).} $J(a,c,f)$ is compactly supported as a function of $c$ in ${\mathbb {C}}^{\times}$, independent on $a$.

{\rm(3).} $J(a,c,f)$ is zero when $|a|$ is small, independent on $c$.

{\rm(4).} $ J(a,c,f) =O(|a|^{2+\varepsilon})$ for any $\varepsilon>0$, when $|a|$ is large, independent on $c$.
nodes.statement_short: $J(a,c,f)$ converges, is compactly supported in $c$, vanishes for small $|a|$ and is $O(|a|^{2+\varepsilon})$ for large $|a|$.
conclusions: $J(a,c,f)$ converges absolutely for all $a,c\in {\mathbb {C}}^{\times}$.
